svg.title: How to read the humidity (psychrometric) chart, air–water at 1 atm
svg.text: How to read the humidity (psychrometric) chart, air–water at 1 atm
Redrawn from the psychrometric equations
Temperature, °F
Humidity 𝓗, lb water vapour per lb dry air
Humid heat c_s, Btu per °F per lb dry air
Volume, ft³ per lb dry air
Adiabatic cooling line
The adiabatic cooling lines on this chart
are (nearly) straight and parallel
Humid heat vs. humidity
Sp. volume dry air
Saturated volume
100% (saturation)
T_wb ≈ 101 °F
Locate the air: dry-bulb temperature on the bottom axis, humidity 𝓗 on the right axis (here 200 °F, 0.02).
Follow the adiabatic-cooling line through the point up to the 100 % (saturation) curve.
Drop to the temperature axis. 4 Read the adiabatic-saturation (= wet-bulb, for air–water) temperature.
Humid heat: from 𝓗 go across to the “humid heat vs. humidity” line, then up to the c_s scale at the top.
Percentage humidity: the curved lines 10 %…100 %; humid volume: the two volume lines read on the left scale.
Redrawn from the equations; in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
